title: Minimum Operations to Break Array Sorting
approach_explanation: The problem asks for the minimum operations required to make an array not sorted. An array is sorted if $a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \dots \leq a_n$. If the array is already not sorted, the answer is $0$. Otherwise, the easiest way to break the sorted property is to violate the non-decreasing order between some adjacent pair $(a_{i}, a_{i+1})$. Increasing the left prefix up to index $i$ by $1$ and decreasing the right suffix from index $i+1$ by $1$ changes the difference $a_{i+1} - a_i$ by $2$. Specifically, applying this operation $k$ times will decrease the difference between $a_{i}$ and $a_{i+1}$ by $2k$. To make $a_{i} > a_{i+1}$, we need the new difference to be strictly less than $0$. Therefore, if the original difference is $d = a_{i+1} - a_i$, the minimum number of operations required for this pair is $\lfloor d / 2 \rfloor + 1$. We take the minimum of this value over all adjacent pairs.

code_breakdown.explanation: Reads the number of test cases $t$ and enters a loop to process each test case individually.
Reads the length $n$ and the elements of the array $a$ into a vector of integers.

Iterates through adjacent elements to check if the array is already unsorted ($a[i] < a[i-1]$). Simultaneously, it tracks the minimum difference $min\_diff$ between any adjacent elements $a[i] - a[i-1]$.

If $min\_diff < 0$, the array is already unsorted, so output $0$. Otherwise, output $(min\_diff / 2) + 1$, which represents the minimum number of operations needed to invert the closest adjacent pair.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: For each testcase, we iterate through the array of length $N$ once to read the input and once to find the minimum adjacent difference. Summing $N$ over all test cases is $\leq 500$, yielding an optimal time complexity well within the 1-second limit.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: A vector of size $N$ is allocated to store the elements for each test case.

strengths: Handles the case where the array is already unsorted correctly by checking negative differences.
Uses optimal linear scan time complexity.
edge_cases_handled: Arrays that are already unsorted ($0$ operations).
Arrays with duplicate adjacent elements ($1 / 2 + 1 = 1$ operation).
best_practices_feedback: Prefer using `std::min` instead of manual `if` comparisons for cleaner code.
